module_title: Advanced Analysis - Types of CPI, IIP, and the GDP Deflator
introduction: This advanced level explores the multiple micro-variants of the CPI used for specific government policies, introduces the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), and explains the ultimate, most comprehensive inflation metric: the GDP Deflator.

core_concepts.title: The 4 Variants of CPI
core_concepts.description:
Because India is vast, different groups have different consumption patterns:
1. CPI-IW (Industrial Workers): Used to calculate 'Dearness Allowance (DA)' for Govt employees. Published by Labour Bureau (Base 2016).
2. CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers) & 3. CPI-RL (Rural Labourers): Published by Labour Bureau.
4. CPI-Combined (Rural + Urban): The main index used by RBI. Published by NSO.

core_concepts.title: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
core_concepts.description: IIP measures the growth rate of different industry groups in the economy (Mining, Manufacturing, and Electricity). It is published monthly by the NSO (Base Year 2011-12).

core_concepts.title: The 8 Core Industries (IIP Backbone)
core_concepts.description: Inside the IIP, there are 8 core infrastructural industries that hold a massive combined weight of '40.27%'. They are (in descending order of weight): Refinery Products (highest), Electricity, Steel, Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Cement, and Fertilizers (lowest).

core_concepts.title: The GDP Deflator
core_concepts.description: Formula: (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100. It is the most comprehensive measure of inflation because, unlike CPI or WPI which only track a limited 'basket' of items, the GDP deflator tracks the price changes of *EVERY SINGLE* domestically produced good and service in the entire country.

important_entities.name: Dearness Allowance (DA)
important_entities.significance: When central government employees protest for a hike in their Dearness Allowance to combat inflation, the government strictly calculates this hike based on the 'CPI-IW (Industrial Workers)' data, not the general headline CPI.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will try to trick you by saying NSO publishes all CPIs. This is FALSE. The NSO only publishes CPI-Urban, CPI-Rural, and CPI-Combined. The specific demographic indices (CPI-IW, CPI-AL, CPI-RL) are published by the 'Labour Bureau' (Ministry of Labour and Employment).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Refinery, Electricity, Steel, Coal. These four hold the maximum weightage among the 8 core industries.

exam_strategy_tips: Knowing that 'Refinery Products' holds the absolute highest weightage among the 8 core industries is a guaranteed mark in major PCS and UPSC prelims.
